summary: Review B (security) of Phase S1 at 6e856e1 found no blocking defect. Step 9 of new-track.md section 2.5 and the standard tell the agent to give the subagent only file paths and project documents. No text tells an agent to pass environment values, secrets, credentials, tokens, or to run a command with untrusted input. run.sh quotes each pattern, has no eval, rejects each pattern with '/' or '..', and runs only regular files below tests/spec_review_gate/. The S1 test scripts write only in mktemp folders. Six nonblocking improvements are recorded.
security_applicability_reason: test-strategy.md section 5, Phase S1, says Review B is applicable with a short scope. The phase diff adds agent prose that starts a subagent (new-track.md step 9, spec-review.md) and an executable bash runner (tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh).
nonblocking_findings: skills/measure/references/new-track.md:302 (same text in claude-skills/measure/references/new-track.md:302): step 9.3 forbids conversation history, questioning answers, and a summary, but it does not name environment values, secrets, credentials, or tokens. No text tells the agent to pass them, so this is not a defect. Recommendation: add 'no environment values, secrets, credentials, or tokens' to the forbidden list. Also say 'the resolved paths of the Product Definition, Tech Stack, and Workflow', because the current sentence does not say paths or contents.

skills/measure/references/spec-review.md:13 with skills/measure/references/new-track.md:303 and :310: the reviewer can search and read the full repository with no limit on secret files such as .env. Step 9.4 writes the returned text without changes into spec-review.md, and step 10 commits it. A reviewer that quotes a secret value puts that value into the git history. Recommendation: add one sentence to Reviewer Input that the reviewer does not quote secret values or credential files, and one check in step 9.4 that the author reads the text for secrets before the commit.

skills/measure/references/new-track.md:306 with skills/measure/references/spec-review.md:116: Round 2 gets the Round 1 author responses, and the 'not fixed' form holds a reason from the user. This is user text beyond the spec files. The text is already part of the committed report, so the exposure does not increase. No change is necessary; record it as known behavior.

tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh:29-35: a pattern such as 'run.sh' or '*.sh' selects run.sh itself as a suite. Probe 'bash tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh run.sh' ran a nested runner with the default patterns, and the outer summary reported '1 suites (PASS=1, FAIL=0)' for two real suites. The nested run stops at one level, because the default patterns do not match run.sh. Recommendation: skip run.sh in the match loop. This is an A3 count risk, not a security defect.

tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh:32: '[ -f "$f" ]' follows symbolic links. A committed symbolic link such as tests/spec_review_gate/test_x.sh that points outside the folder will run. A pattern alone cannot cause this; it needs a committed file. Recommendation: add '[ -L "$f" ] && continue' or document the rule.

tests/spec_review_gate/test_s1_new_track.sh:22 and tests/spec_review_gate/test_s1_standard.sh:19: 'TMP="$(mktemp -d)"' has no failure check. When mktemp fails, TMP is empty and the scripts write to '/diff.out', '/mix/...', and similar paths at the file system root. These paths are outside the repository. Recommendation: add '[ -n "$TMP" ] && [ -d "$TMP" ] || exit 2' after each mktemp call.
evidence: git rev-parse HEAD printed 6e856e18c8fb96c4f2960a95ac96f3ed673058c6, which equals audited_head_sha. git status --short printed only '?? extensions/' (out of scope).

git diff --stat 65c7925..6e856e1: 16 files, 1001 insertions, 17 deletions. The security-relevant files are skills/measure/references/new-track.md, skills/measure/references/spec-review.md, their claude-skills copies, tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh, test_s1_new_track.sh, and test_s1_standard.sh. The other files are prose (CHANGELOG.md, README.md, measure/product.md, measure/tech-stack.md, measure/tracks.md, plan.md, metadata.json) and hold no secret, credential, or token.

Scope item 1: step 9 (new-track.md:299-308) gives the subagent the absolute paths of the standard, spec.md, and plan.md, and the resolved Product Definition, Tech Stack, and Workflow (line 302). It forbids conversation history, questioning answers, and an author summary. Step 9 and spec-review.md contain no instruction to pass environment values, user data beyond the track and project documents, or to run a command. The not-run branch (line 301) writes a fixed string only.

Scope item 2, static read of run.sh: the loop uses 'for pattern in "$@"' (line 19). Line 21 rejects each pattern that contains '/' or '..'. Line 29 expands the pattern as a glob with IFS empty, so a space does not split it. Bash does not do command substitution, brace expansion, tilde expansion, or parameter expansion on the value of a variable, and the script has no eval. A glob without '/' matches only entries of tests/spec_review_gate/. Line 32 keeps only regular files, and lines 33-35 keep only *.sh and *.py names. Lines 53-54 run each suite by the quoted absolute path "$SUITE_DIR/$f".

Scope item 2, live probe 1: 'bash tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh ../test_s1_standard.sh' printed 'ignored pattern (not relative to the suite folder): ../test_s1_standard.sh', 'no suites matched', and exited 1.

Scope item 2, live probe 2: patterns '/etc/passwd', '[.][.]', '{..,x}', 'run sh', '.*', '-n', '', 'test_none;echo INJECTED', 'test_none|echo INJECTED', 'test_none&&echo INJECTED' ran no suite, printed no 'INJECTED', printed 'no suites matched', and exited 1. '/etc/passwd' and '{..,x}' printed the ignored-pattern message.

Scope item 2, live probe 3: patterns '$HOME', '~', '\.\./x.sh', and a pattern with a newline followed by '../x.sh' ran no file outside the folder. '\.\./x.sh' and the newline pattern printed the ignored-pattern message. 'test_s1_*' in the same call ran the two real suites only.
Scope item 2: the harness permission layer rejected a probe call that held '$(...)' and backtick patterns. The static read above covers this case: the runner never evaluates a pattern as code.

Scope item 2: test_s1_new_track.sh:357-363 is a committed probe. It runs a copy of the runner in a temporary tree with '../outside.sh' and an absolute path, and checks that no marker file appears. It passed.

Scope item 3: test_s1_new_track.sh writes only below "$TMP" from mktemp -d (lines 22, 232, 261-264, 293-294, 321-333, 342, 351, 360) and removes it with an EXIT trap (line 23). test_s1_standard.sh writes only below "$TMP" (lines 19-20, 200, 218-246). The real runner call at test_s1_new_track.sh:271 matches no suite and writes nothing. git status --short --ignored tests/ skills/ claude-skills/ measure/ after three full runs printed only the existing ignored entries 'measure/runs/' and 'skills/measure-orchestrator/scripts/__pycache__/'.

Full suite: 'bash tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh test_s1_*' ran test_s1_new_track.sh (41 checks, PASS=41, FAIL=0) and test_s1_standard.sh (16 checks, PASS=16, FAIL=0). The summary was '=== spec_review_gate: 2 suites (PASS=2, FAIL=0) ==='.
A2 (consent-blind publish gate): not applicable. The phase has no draft-to-published status change and no named subject.
A6 (registry overstatement): the diff of measure/tracks.md changes only the track marker from '- [ ]' to '- [~]'. The registry makes no claim that a security state is resolved.
